source:
For production releases, deleting an audit log is prohibited even during an incident.

A staging reset may delete synthetic logs only after the test owner approves; this exception never applies to production.

Emergency production rollback is allowed without a new release review only when it restores the last approved build and preserves audit logs.

Whether third-party archive copies may be erased is unresolved.

This invented policy is version P-8; the example service is named Cedar and has no real deployment endpoint.

questions.text: May an incident responder delete production audit logs using the staging-reset exception?
May an emergency rollback restore the last approved production build without a new release review if audit logs are preserved?
Does this policy authorize erasing third-party archive copies?

plain_message: Production audit logs must survive incidents. Staging synthetic-log deletion needs test-owner approval and does not apply to production. An emergency rollback needs no new release review only if it restores the last approved build and keeps audit logs. Third-party archive erasure is unresolved.
